title: Projective and global dimension are well defined
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $M$ an $R$-module and $m\ge n\ge0$ integers. (1) If $0\to P_n\to\dots\to P_0\to M\to0$ is an exact sequence of $R$-modules with every $P_i$ projective (a projective resolution of $M$ of length $\le n$), then putting $P_i=0$ for $n<i\le m$ gives an exact sequence $0\to P_m\to\dots\to P_0\to M\to0$ with all $P_i$ projective, i.e. a projective resolution of length $\le m$. (2) If $M$ has a projective resolution of length $\le n$ for some $n\ge0$, then there is a least integer $d\ge0$ such that $M$ has a projective resolution of length $\le d$, and for every $k\ge0$: $M$ has a projective resolution of length $\le k$ if and only if $d\le k$. (3) If there is an $n\ge0$ such that every $R$-module has a projective resolution of length $\le n$, then there is a least such integer $g\ge0$, and for every $k\ge0$: every $R$-module has a projective resolution of length $\le k$ if and only if $g\le k$.
